entries.subjective_report: Lap 1 returned to the car because the athlete forgot two 15 g honey sachets. Lap 2 was the real climb to Twin Peaks. Lap 3 was Pure Quill Stage. Lap 5 was 2K+ trail. Lap 6 was the climb out and the last part of DH Line. Lap 7 was a cool-down around the car park. The athlete did not climb Twin Peaks twice because lap 3 felt so good; he chose 2K+ to check whether the feeling transferred. No setup was changed, no root ping occurred, the trail was dry, and the athlete felt strong on the bike.

session_contract_review.technical_quality_notes: Pure Quill felt sufficiently good that the athlete replaced the planned second same-route repetition with 2K+ to check transfer. He reported no root ping and felt strong on the bike. The report does not yet establish the specific body-position, braking, line-choice, fatigue, or late-session outcome on 2K+.
session_contract_review.route_action: one Pure Quill descent followed by 2K+ rather than a second Pure Quill descent or direct egress

coach_contract_audit.actual_test: Pure Quill execution followed by cross-trail transfer check on 2K+
coach_contract_audit.primary_interpretation: Promising rider-adaptation and skill-transfer signal, pending explicit 2K+ technical review.
coach_contract_audit.secondary_confounder: Dry terrain likely increased root friction and predictability and cannot be excluded from the causal interpretation.
coach_contract_audit.setup_interpretation: No setup change means the result cannot be credited to a new setting and does not justify an HSC change.
coach_contract_audit.reason: The route action changed, actual load materially exceeded the prescription, technical review fields remain incomplete, and no explicit valid stop-rule outcome has been supplied.

lap_4_context.terrain: Two steep climbs that the athlete had recently ridden seated but used to ride standing in earlier years.
lap_4_context.execution: Stood for both climbs and pushed them maximally.
lap_4_context.athlete_training_hypothesis: Reintroduce more standing climbing because earlier peak-power performances predate the more road-bike-style seated training emphasis.

post_pure_quill_gate_report.athlete_intent: Felt ready for another Pure Quill but counted the lap 1 detour toward the cap, substituted maximal standing work on the lap 4 climbs, and then rode 2K+.

session_contract_review.technical_quality_notes: The athlete reported that the dynamically centred posture, stable front tracking, brake release, and line choice transferred to 2K+. Confidence was high enough to double some rough sections. There was no late skill fade, reactive braking, delayed line choice, deflection, or near miss. No fork dive or pack-down, rear kick, or pitching was reported. The athlete noticed more two-wheel drifting rather than rear-only drifting; whether this was a controlled balanced drift or reduced grip margin still requires mechanical interpretation.
session_contract_review.tyre_drift_observation: More two-wheel drifting instead of rear-only drifting.
session_contract_review.athlete_stop_rule_statement: None except lap 4 because, after doing lap 1, the athlete did not think he should complete two Pure Quill runs.

coach_contract_audit.lap_4_intensity: RPE 10 materially exceeded the prescribed lap-two climb ceiling of RPE 4 and met the stored downshift threshold.
coach_contract_audit.upper_body_gate: Reported upper-body fatigue of 5/10 exceeded the admission gate of 2/10 and the technical-stop threshold above 3/10; timing within the session remains unreported.
coach_contract_audit.technical_disposition: Clean reported technical execution, but not a clean nominal prescription sample because the route changed and the physiological dose materially exceeded the contract.
coach_contract_audit.stop_rule_disposition: Do not assign a valid stop-rule outcome until the athlete explicitly selects the schema code after reviewing the lap 4 RPE and upper-body thresholds.
coach_contract_audit.fueling_disposition: Fluid rate was within target; carbohydrate and sodium rates were below the stored 90-150-minute Kuala Lumpur MTB targets.

observed_bests.20_min: 222 W in a 2024 indoor session; historical P20, not current FTP.

coach_power_history_audit.today_location_audit: Today's 1001 W peak occurred at the start of lap 5/2K+ at high cadence, not during the lap 4 standing climbs. Lap 4 reached 451 W maximum and represented low-cadence standing torque rather than the activity's peak-power event.
coach_power_history_audit.interpretation: The record supports restoring MTB-specific standing torque and 5-30-second punch exposure, but it does not show that seated aerobic/tempo work failed. Indoor structure produced the best sustained 10-20-minute power, while short-power records were predominantly expressed in MTB activities.
coach_power_history_audit.decision: Rebalance rather than reset: retain one recoverable seated tempo/torque session and later add a controlled standing-climb microdose using repeatable 20-60-second power, traction, form, repeat falloff, and next-day response instead of one-second maximum power.
coach_power_history_audit.confidence: High for dates and current-lap placement; moderate across power-meter eras; low-to-moderate for attributing historical differences specifically to seated versus standing posture.

coach_drift_interpretation.primary_hypothesis: A more dynamically centred posture distributed lateral load more evenly across both tyres instead of overloading or unweighting the rear.
coach_drift_interpretation.positive_validation: Both tyres release together, chassis yaw stays aligned with the intended line, and grip returns progressively without a steering catch.
coach_drift_interpretation.failure_signature: Front-first release, bar tuck, abrupt re-grip, drift beginning under unresolved braking, or a line correction would indicate reduced front-grip margin rather than desirable neutral drift.
coach_drift_interpretation.setup_decision: No suspension change; the absence of dive, pack-down, kick, or pitching does not support adding HSC.

reconciles_prior_report.standing_climb: The post-2K climb ridden standing on 2026-07-09 is the same climb contained in lap 4 on 2026-07-16.
reconciles_prior_report.strength_context: The athlete has also been training squats and lunges.
reconciles_prior_report.fueling: Both honey sachets were consumed; the earlier table listed the nutrition for one sachet, not the number eaten.
reconciles_prior_report.stop_rule: The athlete explicitly supplied a valid schema stop-rule outcome.
reconciles_prior_report.drift: The front tyre initiated the slide; the rear then drifted to match it, and the athlete picked the bike up to restore grip and exit.

2026_07_09_lap_7.punchy_climb_pedaling: 731 seconds at 124.3 W average, 227 W maximum, 8.1 percent average grade and 144.8 bpm average HR.

2026_07_16_lap_4.punchy_climb_pedaling: 424 seconds at 200.6 W average, 428 W maximum, 11.4 percent average grade and 159.6 bpm average HR.

same_climb_comparison.interpretation_guardrail: The same climb identity strengthens specificity, but lap boundaries, selected sections, grade mix, standing duration and effort differed. The comparison supports better standing power expression, not a causal seven-day fitness gain.

session_contract_review.technical_quality_notes: Overall posture transfer and 2K+ execution were strong, with no late fade, reactive braking, delayed line choice or near miss. However, the front tyre initiated a corner drift before the rear matched it. The athlete successfully reduced lean by picking the bike up and restored grip for the exit. This demonstrates a skilled recovery but is not the stable-front-tracking outcome required for a clean nominal technical calibration.
session_contract_review.drift_recovery: Rear drifted into alignment; athlete picked the bike up and grip returned for the corner exit.

coach_interpretation.standing_adaptation: The week-to-week change is primarily improved recruitment and re-access to a previously familiar standing pattern, with squats and lunges as a plausible supporting force-capacity input. It cannot represent large new muscular adaptation in seven days.
coach_interpretation.drift: A front-first release has less safety margin than a simultaneous neutral drift. The recovery was skilled, but the target remains earlier pressure management and a progressive two-tyre release rather than relying on rear drift to rescue front push.
coach_interpretation.setup: Keep suspension unchanged; no evidence supports an HSC increase.
